propositions: The byte-equivalence oracle invokes both production _convert and a copied _legacy_convert for 884 corpus units, doubling Pandoc subprocess calls and coupling the legacy oracle to live production constants instead of immutable expected outputs.

Changing production _PANDOC_TO to plain mutates both production and copied legacy digests identically, proving the copied oracle does not independently pin landed bytes and fails to detect format drift.

The immutable golden fixture schema version 1 recorded a single macOS-arm64 Pandoc binary SHA-256 as platform-independent, causing all three Ubuntu CI jobs to reject the Linux x86_64 binary hash while macOS passed.

The schema version 2 repair retains generating platform and fingerprint metadata, adds a complete darwin-arm64/linux-x86_64 fingerprint map, and selects the correct supported hash by stable platform key to restore cross-platform CI validation.

Replacing the copied _legacy_convert subprocess with immutable fixture lookup preserves all 884 real production _convert Pandoc calls per change while eliminating 884 legacy subprocesses and achieving 49.4 percent paired runtime savings.

A deterministic generator script with version/fingerprint validation and held-out RED→GREEN mutation testing confirms the independent oracle detects production format mutations while timeout and group-reap hardening tests remain covered.
